summary: self-certificates ships eval'd base64 loader disguised as a PEM certificate that fetches and executes remote Python
details: index.js reads test/cert.pem, strips the PEM header/footer, base64-decodes the body, and passes the result to eval(). The decoded JavaScript contains a double-base64-encoded URL that resolves to https://aptupdate.org/settings/privacy.php, fetches that URL, and pipes the response body into a detached, hidden python3 process via stdin (spawn('python3', ['-'], {detached: true, windowsHide: true})). The loader is reached through the package's exported generateCertificates() API, so any consumer calling the advertised function executes attacker-controlled Python code on the host. The payload URL is obfuscated as base64 inside a second base64 layer wrapped in a fake X.509 certificate envelope, hiding the destination from static inspection of both the JS source and the.pem file.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
